Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: photorealistic apartment interior visualization, one individual room image. Output requested exactly 1536x1024 landscape, no collage, no text, no watermark, no people. Delicate material realism, professional interior photograph.

Room: combined living+dining only 面积未公开 total. Keep this exact view from balcony side toward dining/entry: sofa along existing RIGHT wall, wall-mounted television on LEFT, existing opening at left rear, same entrance door at rear right. Replace bulky leather sofa with shallow comfortable charcoal woven sofa, about 2.1m long, slim arms and saddle leather small pillow; no giant blue sofa. Replace heavy central coffee table with exactly two small nesting pewter/oak SIDE tables beside sofa, leaving center and crossing route visibly open. Replace big floor-standing media storage with a very slim wall-mounted fumed-oak media ledge. Quiet textured mineral grey walls with a few medium-brown oak panels, restrained abstract charcoal art, small plum accent. Back dining zone has modest rectangular extendable fumed-oak table and four lightweight charcoal upholstered chairs, simple brushed nickel compact pendant, slim shallow entrance cabinet. Grey mineral floor and compact charcoal woven rug. Preserve compact depth, modest ceiling and all original wall/door structure; no new partitions or enormous vacant floors.

observed: Original sofa-right, TV-left, dining-back arrangement and structural openings retained.
Charcoal woven sofa, slim media ledge and two small nesting tables; center route open.

Therefore the SAME shallow charcoal woven sofa now appears along the LEFT wall, with same saddle leather cushion and small plum cushion, same tall restrained abstract artwork above it, same two little nesting pewter/oak side tables close beside sofa and an open center crossing. The SAME wall-mounted TV and very slim fumed-oak floating media ledge now appear on RIGHT wall. The same one upright charcoal chair with oak arms and narrow pewter side table stay at the balcony's RIGHT short-end corner as viewed from this camera, central balcony floor entirely open.
